fixes.explanation: That's right, baker. While Peter is still reflecting, the Spirit speaks up. The Spirit says, "Behold, three men are looking for you." (Acts 10:19). And He knows the exact number of men at the gate.
That's the one, baker. Cornelius, the centurion in Caesarea, "…gave generously to the people and prayed to God regularly." (Acts 10:2). His faith had open hands and bent knees.

That one sounds official, friend, but it isn't in the passage. Acts 10:2 says Cornelius gave generously to the people and prayed to God regularly. There's no weekly study session with the priests in the text. The writer sticks to his generosity and his prayers.

That's him, baker. The angel says, "Now send men to Joppa to call for a man named Simon who is called Peter." (Acts 10:5). He goes by two names here, and the angel gives both. That's a handy thing when more than one Simon is around.
Hiding would make it a different story, baker. Acts 10:9 says Peter "…went up on the roof to pray." Nothing in the text says he's ducking anybody.
That's the sheet, baker. It "…contained all kinds of four-footed animals and reptiles of the earth, as well as birds of the air." (Acts 10:12). It's a full zoo in a bedsheet.

Scrolls would be a neat delivery, baker. But that isn't what's in the sheet. It "…contained all kinds of four-footed animals and reptiles of the earth, as well as birds of the air." (Acts 10:12). No scrolls are mentioned in the passage.

That's a careful answer, friend, but it isn't what Peter says. He answers, "No, Lord!" and "I have never eaten anything impure or unclean." (Acts 10:14). The text has him answer the voice himself, with no one else asked.
I like the story, but the Spirit never gives that reason. The reason He gives is, "…because I have sent them." (Acts 10:20). Peter even asks the men, "Why have you come?" (Acts 10:21).

Yes. Acts 10:23 says, "…the next day he got ready and went with them, accompanied by some of the brothers from Joppa." Peter goes with the three men, and some brothers come along too. Peter doesn't make the trip alone.
